items.q: What is delta.seconds for delta = datetime.timedelta(days=11, hours=10, minutes=9, seconds=8)?
rationales: 986948.0 is total_seconds(), which includes the 11 days.
8 forgets the hours and minutes; the seconds attribute holds everything below a whole day.

items.q: Under Python 3.14.4, what year does datetime.datetime.strptime("January of '69", "%B of '%y") give?
rationales: The chapter's table says %y spans 1970 to 2069, but the values 69 to 99 map to 1969 to 1999.
A datetime always has a four-digit year.

items.q: A computer in the Pacific zone reads 11:04 PM on 17 March 2026. Which hour does time.ctime() print?
rationales: ctime uses a 24-hour clock, so the book's 11:05:38 cannot have been printed at 11 PM.
ctime prints no AM or PM.

items.q: Which call measures how long a block of code takes without being fooled when someone sets the system clock back?
rationales: time.time() reads the system clock, which can be set back, so a later reading can be smaller.
ctime gives a text, not a number to subtract.

items.q: What does subprocess.run(['python', '-c', 'print(1)']) return when the program ends?
options: A CompletedProcess recording the arguments and the return code
rationales: The text is kept only with capture_output=True, and then in the stdout attribute of the result.
run waits for the program and returns a CompletedProcess; Popen is what you use to keep going alongside.

items.q: A Popen child is still running. What does its poll() return?
rationales: 0 is the exit code of a child that has ended without error.
poll() returns None or the exit code, never a Boolean.

items.q: On Linux, what return code does a child show after its Popen object's kill() ended it?
rationales: 0 would mean it finished without error; kill sends SIGKILL, signal 9, and a negative code means a signal ended the child.
1 is the usual code of a program that failed by itself.
A naive and an aware datetime are never equal.
Only ordering them with < or > raises TypeError; == just returns False.

items.q: Which call raises a DeprecationWarning under Python 3.14.4?
rationales: This is the recommended replacement for utcnow().
now() without a zone is not deprecated; it returns a naive local time.
Sunday was 6 January 2019.
Tuesday was 8 January 2019.

items.q: What does subprocess.run('echo x; echo INJECTED', shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split() give?
rationales: split() cuts the text at every space, so one long item cannot result; even with the text quoted by shlex.quote the list is ['x;', 'echo', 'INJECTED'].
The shell ran a second command after the semicolon, so INJECTED is printed too.
